messages.subject: Spectronaut file format requirements do not match documentation
messages.subject_clean: Spectronaut file format requirements do not match documentation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I tried to run MSStats4.4.1 with a DIA export from Spectronaut, but apparently headers are incompatible. In contrast to what is stated in the documentation, MSStats still seems to use a very old export format from Spectronaut as template (e.g. ProteinName is not recognized as column header but ProteinAccessions is required as proper input when I cross-check with the run example provided). There seems to to be the same issue for MSStatsShiny. Could you please check?
Thank you,
Sandra

messages.subject: dataProcess unable to complete
messages.body_plain:
I've been using the MSstats.csv output from fragpipe for my unlabeled DDA MSstats analysis for a while now, but for some reason with my most recent data set the dataProcess function just seems to stall no matter how long I leave it. When I say stalls I mean on the 'Start the summarization per subplot...' step it doesn't get past 1%. However, the task manager still shows that my R session is actively using CPU and memory, so I know it's not frozen. If I take a smaller subset of the data (100,000 features) it stalls at the same place but at 6%. I've troubleshooted by restarting R, my PC, updating all packages, checking that I have the most recent MSstats version, and re-running the analysis on a similar data set (which worked as expected). I attached the log file and a sample of the fragpipe output data. I'm wondering If i overlooked something obvious?

I appreciate the help,
Scott

messages.subject: Re: dataProcess unable to complete
messages.body_plain:
Okay So the issue it turns out was RAM. After looking around on the forms I found the one "MSstats::dataProcess RAM overflow for SpectroNaut input" very useful. The difficult part was that I didn't get any error telling me what the possible issue could be. After following Christian Schori suggestion of setting the R_MAX_VSIZE to a higher value, with no luck, I followed his later suggestion of setting the "featureSubset" argument in dataProcess to "topN", then setting "n_top_feature" = 1000. The processing step looked like it initially stalled but after a few minutes was able to finish.

Thank you past Christian

messages.subject: Strange Log2fc values
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I noticed an outlier log2fc value for a protein in the finished report. I think I have traced it back to a very large imputed abundance for a peptide.

> select(quantdata$FeatureLevelData %>% filter(PROTEIN == "P21912"), GROUP, RUN , censored, INTENSITY, ABUNDANCE, newABUNDANCE, predicted)
   GROUP RUN censored INTENSITY ABUNDANCE newABUNDANCE predicted
1      A   1    FALSE  12436600  23.46295     23.46295        NA
2      A   2    FALSE  17163400  24.13429     24.13429        NA
3      B   3     TRUE        NA        NA    296.37264  296.3726

Does anyone know why this is happening and/or what I can do to prevent this in the future? There are a total of three peptides with high imputed values. My dataProcess options are

  logTrans = 2,
  normalization = 'equalizeMedians',
  summaryMethod = 'TMP',
  MBimpute = TRUE,
  censoredInt='NA',
  maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999

Thank you,
-Chris

Thank you for your response, Mateusz.

Based on your hint, I tried replacing the full path of the file, in the filename column with just the filename (so as to avoid '/' character).
But that didn't make a difference

Please find below link to modified version of subset of the data
https://drive.google.com/file/d/17PYnx1xbcBc7hG1gElUn7QAgm7_HD6er/view?usp=sharing

MSstats 4.4.1 as seen previously reported same error in SkylinetoMSstatsFormat step itself, MSstats 3.18.5 gave duplicates error in the 2nd step.
To resolve this I tried,

data <- SkylinetoMSstatsFormat(data)

data.processed <- data %>% group_by(BioReplicate, ProteinName,

                                      PeptideSequence, PrecursorCharge,
                                      FragmentIon, ProductCharge) %>%

    slice_min(order_by = DetectionQValue, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup()

data_process_output <- dataProcess(data, logTrans = 2, normalization = FALSE, censoredInt = '0', remove50missing = FALSE)

This did work (only in MSstats 3.18.5), but I'm not really sure if I should be filtering like this based on Q-value.

Looking forward to your feedback :)
